title: Spain Probes Indian Visa Giant BLS International Over Alleged Schengen Fraud Network in Algeria
excerpt: Spanish authorities expand consulate visa fraud investigation to include India-listed outsourcing firm that processes applications across 46 countries.
body:
• Spanish authorities are investigating BLS International's role in an alleged visa fraud network linked to the Spanish consulate in Algiers, where applicants were reportedly charged up to €25,000 for Schengen visas.
  • Spain's National Court arrested the vice consul of the Spanish consulate in Algeria and an Algerian worker earlier this year over the scheme, which allegedly laundered proceeds through vehicle purchases in Spain.
  • BLS International, a Delhi-listed firm operating in over 66 countries, holds Spain's global visa outsourcing contract covering more than 120 centers across Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Americas.
  • The company was already debarred by India's Ministry of External Affairs in October 2025 for two years over allegations of extortion, malpractice, and unfair trade practices affecting passport applicants.

Spanish Probe Expands to Visa Outsourcing Partner

Spain's judicial investigation into a visa fraud ring operating through its consulate in Algeria has expanded to include BLS International Services Ltd., the Indian company that holds the global contract for processing Spanish visa applications, according to multiple Indian media reports.

The probe centers on an alleged network that facilitated Schengen visas through the Spanish consulate in Algiers in exchange for payments as high as €25,000 — a staggering markup over the standard €80 processing fee. NDTV reported that the investigation widened to include BLS International after Spanish officials at the consulate were arrested.

Spain's National Court, under Judge María Tardón of Central Court of Instruction No. 3, is leading the investigation. The Economic and Fiscal Crime Unit (UDEF) of Spain's National Police arrested Vicente Moreno, the number two official at the Spanish consulate in Algiers, along with an Algerian worker, after detecting both suspects were in Spain, according to reports from EL PAÍS confirmed by Spanish legal sources.

" There is an inspection ongoing and the department is waiting for judicial notification to adopt all the appropriate measures provided for in these cases."

— Spain's Ministry of Foreign Affairs

Laundering Through Vehicle Purchases

Investigators believe the network operated by facilitating visa issuance from the Spanish consulate in exchange for money, with proceeds allegedly laundered in Spain through vehicle purchases and potentially other mechanisms, according to the reporting. Searches were conducted at locations in Sagunto (Valencia) and Torrevieja (Alicante). Both detainees were provisionally released after appearing before the judge by videoconference.

The investigation also involves agents from Spain's Central Unit of Illegal Immigration Networks and Documentary Falsities (UCRIF) and the Deputy Directorate of Customs Surveillance (DAVA), indicating authorities suspect broader connections to human trafficking and irregular immigration networks.

BLS International: A Company Under Pressure

BLS International Services Ltd., headquartered in Delhi and listed on Indian stock exchanges with a market capitalization of approximately ₹20,000 crore, processes visa applications for over 46 governments worldwide. The company's partnership with Spain, first established in 2017 through a five-year contract worth €175 million, was renewed to include national visa applications and covers more than 120 visa centers globally. In Algeria specifically, BLS operates Spain's visa application centers in both Algiers and Oran.

The Spanish probe adds to a growing list of controversies for the company. In October 2025, India's Ministry of External Affairs debarred BLS International from participating in new government tenders for two years, citing "allegations including court cases and multiple complaints from passport applicants." The MEA debarment triggered an 18% single-day drop in BLS shares. Joint Managing Director Shikhar Aggarwal said at the time that existing contracts were unaffected.

Algeria's Visa Fraud Problem

The Spanish consulate case emerges against a backdrop of widespread visa fraud targeting Algerian nationals seeking to enter Europe. In a separate case uncovered in 2024, Algerian authorities dismantled a travel agency that sold forged Schengen visas for France and Spain at prices ranging from €3,300 to over €5,300 per application.

Algeria ranked sixth globally in Schengen visa applications in 2024, with its citizens submitting over 544,600 applications. Of these, approximately 340,780 were approved while 185,101 were rejected, with France and Spain receiving the bulk of applications. The high rejection rate and limited appointment availability have created fertile ground for fraud networks.

What's at Stake for Indian Visa Applicants

For the Indian diaspora, the developments underscore risks in the visa outsourcing model that millions rely on annually. BLS International processes Indian passport and visa applications in Canada, the United States, the Middle East, and dozens of other countries. A 2025 CBC News investigation in Canada documented complaints about "premium lounge" overcharges and forced add-on services at BLS centers serving the Indian community.

BLS International has not publicly commented on the Spanish investigation. The company has previously stated it cooperates with all regulatory authorities and that its operations meet the highest standards of compliance.

What's Next

The Spanish judicial investigation remains ongoing, with Judge Tardón's court examining the full scope of the alleged fraud network. Spain's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has signaled that appropriate measures — including potential dismissal of the vice consul — will follow once judicial notifications are received. For BLS International, the outcome could affect its €175 million Spanish contract, one of its largest Schengen partnerships, at a time when the company is already navigating its MEA debarment in India.
